note: Short neutral paraphrases of each party's publicly stated priorities for the 2026 Victorian state election, drawn from the parties' own websites and announcements. Not endorsements. Policies evolve — the party's own website is canonical. Blank cells mean the party has made no major public commitment on that issue specific to Victoria 2026.

positions.Labor: Continue delivering the Big Housing Build; focus on social and affordable housing supply; planning reform to unlock density near transport.
positions.Coalition: Reduce planning red tape to speed private supply; opposes some density-near-transport mandates; emphasises first-home-buyer support.
positions.Greens: Massive public housing expansion; permanent renters' rights (indefinite leases, rent caps); end no-grounds evictions; levy on vacant properties.
positions.One Nation: Argues housing pressure is driven by immigration; proposes migration cuts as primary policy lever.
positions.Victorian Socialists: Build hundreds of thousands of public housing units; universal rent control; take over major developers; end homelessness as a priority.
positions.Family First: Support for home ownership and larger family-friendly housing; opposes high-density mandates perceived as changing suburban character.

positions.Labor: Target 95% renewable electricity by 2035; State Electricity Commission expansion; offshore wind; EV incentives.
positions.Coalition: Energy policy focused on reliability and cost; sceptical of some renewables targets; openness to gas as a transition fuel.
positions.Greens: Faster coal exit (2030); community-owned renewables; expanded national parks; strong anti-logging and anti-fossil-fuel stance.
positions.One Nation: Sceptical of climate action's economic costs; opposes net-zero mandates; supports coal and gas; opposes wind farms.
positions.Victorian Socialists: Public ownership of energy; rapid, worker-led transition to renewables; nationalise fossil fuel assets; expand public transport over roads.
positions.Family First: Climate not a core focus; opposes measures seen as raising cost of living; support for traditional energy.

positions.Labor: Continued hospital infrastructure investment; women's health focus; mental health reforms post-Royal Commission; GP respite clinics.
positions.Coalition: Reduce elective-surgery waiting lists; opposes some management structures; emphasises frontline over bureaucracy.
positions.Greens: Free dental in Medicare (state advocacy); public hospitals fully funded; mental health care parity; harm-reduction drug policy.
positions.One Nation: Opposes vaccine mandates; supports choice in medical treatment; concerns about health system staffing from migration policy.
positions.Victorian Socialists: Free universal public healthcare; nationalise private hospitals; mass hiring of nurses; abolish private health subsidies.
positions.Family First: Protection of conscience objections for health workers; opposition to voluntary assisted dying expansion; pro-life stance on abortion.

positions.Labor: Free kinder for 3- and 4-year-olds; continued public school funding uplift; TAFE free courses; teacher recruitment incentives.
positions.Coalition: Back-to-basics curriculum; phonics; discipline reforms; more parental choice; opposes some gender-identity classroom content.
positions.Greens: Fully fund public schools to Gonski 100%; free TAFE and university; reduce class sizes; lift teacher pay substantially.
positions.One Nation: Opposes 'woke curriculum'; return to traditional subjects; religious freedom in schools.
positions.Victorian Socialists: Nationalise private schools; cancel student debt; free universal childcare; abolish ATAR and school rankings.
positions.Family First: Parental authority in education; religious schools' freedom to hire; opt-out from gender-identity curriculum; home-schooling support.

positions.Labor: Suburban Rail Loop (SRL) delivery; Metro Tunnel operation; level crossing removals; EV charging rollout; airport rail commitment.
positions.Coalition: Opposes SRL in current form (cost); emphasise road investment; faster regional rail; review major-project procurement.
positions.Greens: Scrap SRL and divert funds to buses, trams, cycling, and local rail electrification; stop urban freeway expansion; free public transport.
positions.One Nation: Focus on roads and highways; opposes congestion-pricing; sceptical of rail megaprojects.
positions.Victorian Socialists: Free public transport; nationalise V/Line and franchised services; massive expansion of trams, trains, buses; stop road widening.
positions.Family First: Prioritise road capacity for families; opposition to some congestion-reduction measures that limit car access.

positions.Labor: Energy bill relief payments; power saving bonus continuation; cheaper public transport fares; cost-of-living package in last budget.
positions.Coalition: Cut state taxes and levies; opposes Vic-specific property taxes; emphasis on cost-of-doing-business for small employers.
positions.Greens: Cut the cost of essentials by public ownership (energy, housing); dental in Medicare; rent caps; levy on big corporations.
positions.One Nation: Blames inflation on immigration and energy policy; supports migration cut and energy mix change.
positions.Victorian Socialists: Big wage rises funded by taxing the wealthy; price controls on essentials; free public services (transport, childcare, dental).
positions.Family First: Family tax relief; support for single-income households; opposes some green levies seen as raising household bills.

positions.Labor: Youth justice reform balancing diversion and accountability; stronger stalking/DV laws; expanded police resources.
positions.Coalition: Tougher bail laws; mandatory minimum sentences for some offences; opposition to raising the age of criminal responsibility.
positions.Greens: Raise the age of criminal responsibility to 14; invest in diversion and treatment over incarceration; address root causes of crime.
positions.One Nation: Tougher sentencing; prison expansion; more police; opposition to decriminalisation policies.
positions.Victorian Socialists: Defund police expansion; invest in community services and mental health; abolish youth prisons.
positions.Family First: Tougher penalties for violent crime; victim-focused justice; religious freedom protections against discrimination claims.

positions.Labor: Continue the Treaty process via the First Peoples' Assembly; implement Yoorrook Justice Commission recommendations.
positions.Coalition: Withdrew support for Treaty in 2024; opposes a statewide treaty framework; favours practical reconciliation over structural reforms.
positions.Greens: Full treaty implementation; truth-telling; return of Crown lands; strong backing for Yoorrook recommendations.
positions.One Nation: Opposes Treaty; opposes race-based policy; argues for formal equality in all public programs.
positions.Victorian Socialists: Support for Treaty, land back, reparations, and sovereignty; supports Yoorrook in full.
positions.Family First: Generally cool to Treaty; emphasises individual rather than group-based rights.
